name: Poor Man's Covered Call (PMCC)
summary: Buy a deep-ITM long-dated call (LEAPS) as a stock surrogate and sell a short-dated OTM call against it, repeating monthly; a covered call at roughly a quarter of the capital.

legs.strike_rule: Deep ITM by delta 0.80-0.90 (never below 0.70 - a lower-delta long tracks the stock too poorly and decays too fast). Extrinsic value of the LEAPS should be <= 10% of its total premium.

OTM by delta 0.20-0.30. HARD CONSTRAINT: short strike >= long strike + net debit per share, so that a both-ITM finish still nets a profit. If no strike satisfies this at delta 0.20-0.30, move the short further out in time rather than violating it.
legs.dte_rule: front leg, 21-45 DTE; 30-35 DTE is the sweet spot

max_profit: At or above the short strike at front expiry: approximately (short strike - long strike) x 100 - net debit + cumulative credits collected from all short calls sold to date. Each successful roll raises this ceiling.
max_loss: The net debit paid, less all credits collected, realized if the underlying collapses and the LEAPS goes to near zero. On a 0.85-delta LEAPS the practical loss curve tracks about 85% of the stock's decline in the near term.
breakevens: Approximately long strike + net debit per share at the LEAPS' expiry; at the short's front expiry the breakeven is lower because the LEAPS retains time value. Each collected credit lowers it further.

greeks.delta: net positive +0.50 to +0.65 per unit (0.85 long minus 0.25 short)
greeks.gamma: slightly negative (the short front call has more gamma than the LEAPS)
greeks.theta: positive but modest, +$1 to +$5/day per unit; the short's decay exceeds the LEAPS' decay
greeks.vega: net positive - LEAPS vega is far larger than the short's; the position is quietly long volatility, which hurts in a vol crush

when_to_use: Bullish 6-24 month view on a quality underlying with a healthy uptrend (spot > 50-day SMA > 200-day SMA). Buy the LEAPS when IV rank is LOW (< 35) so you are not overpaying for the long leg's vega; sell the short calls when the front-month IV is relatively elevated. On a $50k account, PMCC is the capital-efficient way to run covered-call income on 5-10 underlyings that would otherwise require $500k of stock.
typical_dte: long 270-730 DTE, short 21-45 DTE, rolled monthly
entry_rules: Trend filter: spot > 50-day SMA AND 50-day SMA > 200-day SMA; underlying must not have declined more than 15% in the last 20 sessions.
IV rank < 35 at the time of the LEAPS purchase (the long leg is your biggest vega exposure).
LEAPS: delta 0.80-0.90, DTE >= 180 (270-730 preferred), extrinsic <= 10% of premium.
MANDATORY: short strike >= long strike + net debit per share. If violated, the trade is rejected.
Net debit per unit <= 5% of equity ($2,500 on a $50k account); no more than 5 concurrent PMCCs.
LEAPS bid-ask <= 5% of its mid; short-call bid-ask <= $0.05.

LEVEL 3 OK: the short call is at a higher strike and an earlier expiry than a long call the account owns - a textbook covered diagonal. Submit as a 2-leg mleg for the open; thereafter manage the short leg as single-leg orders. If legging the open, BUY THE LEAPS FIRST and only then sell the call.
management_rules: Close the short call at 50-75% of the credit received, then immediately sell the next cycle's 0.20-0.30 delta call at 21-45 DTE. This roll cadence is the income engine.

If the short call's |delta| exceeds 0.50, roll it up and out for a NET CREDIT only, and only to a strike still >= long strike + remaining net debit. If no credit roll satisfies that, close the short and let the LEAPS run naked-long (which is allowed and has no assignment risk) until a valid strike appears.
Roll the LEAPS forward when its delta falls below 0.70 OR its DTE falls below 120 - inside 90 DTE the theta cliff accelerates sharply.
Hard stop on the LEAPS: close the whole position if the LEAPS' mark falls to 50% of the purchase price, or if spot closes below the 200-day SMA for 3 consecutive sessions.
Track cost basis: the running net debit = original debit - cumulative credits. Every management decision references the CURRENT net debit, not the original.
Never sell more short calls than LEAPS owned - a second short call is naked and would require level 4.
exit_rules: Close or roll the short call by 14:30 ET on its expiration day, unconditionally. A PMCC short call that expires ITM means -100 shares delivered on Monday.
Close the short call immediately if its extrinsic value <= $0.05/share or |delta| >= 0.90.

Close the short call before the close of the session preceding ex-dividend whenever its extrinsic value < the declared dividend per share. This is the #1 cause of PMCC assignment, and it typically happens when the stock has rallied through the short strike.
Close the LEAPS no later than 90 DTE, and always after the short call has been bought back.
Full exit: buy back the short call FIRST, then sell the LEAPS. Never the reverse.
If assigned: buy back the 100 short shares at market on the next open, keep the LEAPS, and re-sell a new short call once the strike constraint is satisfiable again.
assignment_risk: Only the short call. Since the long strike is well below the short strike, an assignment produces -100 shares fully covered by a deep-ITM long call - economically similar to having exercised the LEAPS, but it leaves the account short stock with borrow and dividend liability. The dominant trigger is ex-dividend: a short call whose extrinsic is less than the dividend will be exercised the night before the ex-date. Do NOT solve the problem by exercising the LEAPS - that throws away its remaining time value; buy the shares back instead.
buying_power: Net debit only. Alpaca recognizes a long call at a lower strike with a later expiry as full cover for the short call, so there is no additional maintenance requirement. If assigned, the short stock position carries a real margin requirement until flattened.
liquidity_needs: LEAPS liquidity is the binding constraint: OI >= 100 at the chosen deep-ITM strike, bid-ask <= 5% of mid, and a real two-sided market. Practically this restricts PMCC to large-cap names and major ETFs (SPY, QQQ, AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, AMD, GOOGL, XLF, etc.). Underlying ADV >= 3M shares.
common_mistakes: Buying a long call with delta below 0.70 (it behaves like a lottery ticket, not stock); selling a short strike below long strike + debit so that a strong rally produces a LOSS; exercising the LEAPS to cover an assignment and throwing away extrinsic value; holding the LEAPS inside 90 DTE; rolling the short for a debit to 'avoid' assignment; buying the LEAPS at high IV rank and watching the long vega bleed; running PMCC on a downtrending stock - the short call premium never compensates for a falling LEAPS.
zero_dte_notes: The short leg is never sold at 0DTE in this playbook (minimum 21 DTE at entry). Weekly short calls at 7 DTE are a valid aggressive variant but raise assignment frequency and gamma risk materially; if used, the 14:30 ET forced close applies every Friday.
family: Calendar and diagonal spreads (time spreads): same-strike calendars, different-strike diagonals, double/triple calendars, double diagonals, PMCC and its put mirror, LEAPS diagonals, calendarized straddles/butterflies, ratio time spreads, and the reverse (short) time spreads
